input.body:
Address: 9 Birch Close, Croydon, CR0 7EX
Ref: TKT-CA0F52

Hi Marcus,

The tenant of this property has reported the following:
Request description: "Boiler is making a loud banging noise and the radiators upstairs are cold. Hot water still works. Not urgent but it's been a week now and it's getting colder."

What we are doing within your £150 limit: arranging a diagnostic visit from a Gas Safe registered engineer, GasSure London (call-out £140). We will confirm the date once the tenants confirm access.

What needs your written approval (please reply by email):
1. Gas safety certificate: our records show the CP12 for the property EXPIRED on 30 September 2026. An annual gas safety check is a legal requirement for the landlord. GasSure London did last year's check (£80). We propose they renew it at the same visit. Total for the visit approx. £220 (£140 call-out + approx. £80 CP12), which is over your £150 limit. Can you please confirm you approve?
2. Any repair the engineer finds will be quoted and sent to you for approval before any work over your limit goes ahead.

Because the gas safety check is overdue, please reply as soon as you can. If you would rather use your own Gas Safe engineer for the certificate, let us know and send us the certificate once it is done.

As you asked, we will contact you by email only.

Kind regards,
Maintenance team

Hello Sadie, this is the maintenance team about your boiler report (ref TKT-CA0F52). We are arranging a Gas Safe engineer, GasSure London, to look at it. They have slots on Mon 12 Oct, 9-11am or 2-4pm. Can you or Tom give access in either slot? Please reply with which one, or tell us if neither works. If you smell gas or a CO alarm goes off, open the windows, don't use switches, leave the house and call 0800 111 999. If you have pets, please tell us.

Dear Tom and Sadie,

Re: 9 Birch Close, boiler banging and upstairs radiators cold (ref TKT-CA0F52)

Thank you for reporting this. We have logged it as urgent. Our maintenance provider GasSure London, a Gas Safe registered engineer, will attend to find out what is wrong with the boiler.

They have these appointments available on Monday 12 October 2026:
- 9:00 to 11:00
- 14:00 to 16:00

We know you both usually work during the day. Please reply and tell us which slot you can do, or if neither works (for example, an evening or a Saturday). We will only book it once you confirm. The engineer may also carry out the annual gas safety check during the same visit.

Until then: hot water still works, so keep using it as normal. If the banging gets worse, turn the boiler off. If you ever smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm goes off, open the windows, don't use any electrical switches, leave the house and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

If you have any pets, please tell us so we can let the engineer know.

Kind regards,
Maintenance team

model_notes:
I've opened ticket TKT-CA0F52 for 9 Birch Close (PROP-0077), but no engineer is booked yet: I'm waiting for the tenants to confirm they can let the engineer in. I've also escalated the expired gas safety certificate to compliance.

**What's wrong:** Sadie Reilly reported the boiler banging loudly and the upstairs radiators cold for about a week; hot water still works. I've marked it **urgent**. It's a partial loss of heating, it's October (before the 1 Nov winter rule) and nobody vulnerable is recorded. There's no gas smell or carbon monoxide alarm, so the gas emergency rules don't apply. The tenancy is active and the property, tenants and landlord details all match the records.

**Something not in the report:** the property's gas safety certificate ran out on 30 Sep 2026, nine days ago. The annual check is a legal requirement.

**Landlord rules:** his 6 Oct email and his property record say the same thing. Nothing over £150 without his written OK, he's abroad until 20 Oct, and email only. His phone number is on file but I haven't used it.

**What I did:**
- **Engineer:** I tried Thames Heating first (best rated, £120 call-out), but their booking system timed out twice. GasSure London are Gas Safe registered and did last year's gas safety check. Their £140 call-out is under the landlord's £150 limit, so the diagnostic visit doesn't need his approval. They're free on Mon 12 Oct, 9–11am or 2–4pm.
- **Tenants:** both slots fall in working hours, and the records say the tenants can only give access after 5pm or on Saturdays. So I asked them to confirm a slot before booking: a text to Sadie (no email on file) and an email to Tom. Both also got the gas emergency advice (0800 111 999) and a reminder to mention pets.
- **Landlord:** I raised approval request APR-54BB6C and emailed him. It asks for his written OK for GasSure to renew the gas safety certificate at the same visit (about £80, so about £220 for the visit). Any repair the engineer finds will be quoted to him before work goes ahead.
- **Compliance:** I escalated the expired certificate as high priority (ESC-FDA1A3) with a full handover. It's a legal duty, the landlord is hard to reach, and someone needs to decide what happens if he doesn't reply.
- **Case status:** set to waiting for tenant, with an internal note on the triage, the Thames failure and why I picked GasSure.

**Next steps:**
1. **If the tenants confirm a slot:** book it with GasSure London and send the appointment confirmation.
2. **If neither slot works:** ask GasSure for an evening or Saturday, or try Thames Heating again.
3. **Chase dates:** tenants Sun 11 Oct, landlord Tue 13 Oct (email only).
4. **Compliance:** decide whether the agency goes ahead with the gas safety check if the landlord stays silent. Done as a separate job (about £80) it would be under his limit.
5. **Repair cost:** the boiler is 11 years old. If the repair quote is high, suggest the landlord gets a replacement assessment.
